title: Exec decision canvas and operational readout pulse
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Purpose: Create a concise, decision-oriented exec readout artifact that combines a lightweight decision canvas with an operational 'pulse' for the roadmap slice covering inference-economics, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployment readiness. This ticket tracks preparation, stakeholder feedback, and the final ask to execs for budget and risk tolerances.
acceptance_criteria: One-page decision canvas summarizing options, tradeoffs, and recommended ask
Operational pulse with 4 SLO metrics and trend sparkline links
A short rollback/runbook lane with trigger thresholds and owners
Stakeholder alignment notes from Eng, Design, Security, and Sales
Finalized exec slide deck + one-pager distributed 48 hours before readout
background: Over the last two quarters we have seen divergent cost trends between hosted and Dedicated customers for medium-length chat workloads. Platform telemetry shows increased KV cache churn and suboptimal batching for a subset of models, which is inflating unit cost by ~12% on peak windows. This readout synthesizes engineering signals, business economics, and the residual risks for the roadmap choices we must signal to execs and board members.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Draft decision canvas completed (v0.1). Focused on three levers: batching/autoscale configs, model quantization profile rollout, and Dedicated capacity commit size.
2026-02-27: Eng ran A/B simulation for aggressive KV caching config; median token latency unchanged, p95 improved 8%. Added cost projection table.
2026-03-03: Design prototype for one-pager and slide skeleton created; Design provided feedback to simplify charts for exec consumption.
2026-03-07: Security review checkpoint — no new data-sharing requirements but recommended tighter audit log wording for Private deploy ask.
2026-03-11: Finance validated expected ROI on 20% infra reallocation for Dedicated; break-even in ~9 months under conservative adoption assumptions. Deck updated.

2026-03-12: Internal dry-run with Eng + Sales; major feedback: add explicit fallback lane for global capacity contention and specify canary rollout thresholds. Status: In Review before exec distribution.
stakeholder_comments: Lead Eng (Priya Rao): 'We need to be explicit about latency SLOs per customer tier. Add a p50/p95/p99 table and clarify compensating ops effort.'
Design (Evan Liu): 'Slides look dense at v0.2 — recommend converting a chart to an annotated timeline for rollout.'
Sales (Carla Mendes): 'Include customer examples that lose throughput under current configs; supports urgency for Dedicated capacity ask.'
Security (Liam O'Connor): 'Audit log phrasing updated per compliance checklist; please include retention SLAs in appendix.'
options_evaluated: Do nothing: continue current config, monitor cost drift (low engineering effort, high economic risk)
Conservative ops: tuned batching + targeted prefix cache persistence for top 10% workloads (medium effort, medium benefit)
Accelerated Dedicated push: fund 20% infra reallocation to expand Dedicated pools + guided migration incentives for high-volume customers (high effort, high benefit)
Product-first optimization: invest in quantized model variants and runtime kernel path improvements (high engineering work, durable cost improvements)
recommended_ask: Approve a time-bound infra reallocation of up to 20% of the Dedicated investment fund (Q2-Q3) to accelerate capacity for high-throughput tenants, plus authority to run a targeted incentive for customer migration. Also approve a small ring-fenced engineering allocation (1.5 FTE quarters) to finalize the quantized model rollout plan and productionize the KV cache persistence experiment.
risk_register: Capacity mismatch: If adoption is slower than forecast, we may leave idle Dedicated capacity for the quarter (mitigation: step-down schedule and secondary burst marketplace).
Quality regression: Quantization rollout may introduce hallucination regressions on small prompt families (mitigation: gated eval suites and automatic regression alerts tied to canary traffic).
Compliance: Private deployments require KMS alignment for new key rotations (mitigation: security-approved appendix and upgrade window).
runbook_and_rollback: Trigger: >5% increase in customer error rate or >10% increase in p95 latency during canary window
Action: Immediate rollback to previous model variant and KV cache config, notify SRE and Customer Success
Owner: Eng Ops (oncall) + PM escalation lead
Communication: Prewritten postmortem template and customer notification draft in appendix
